speaker: Dana
text: Hi Ravi, thanks for coming in. Did you find the office alright?

speaker: Ravi
text: Yes, though the traffic on the bridge was terrible this morning.

speaker: Dana
text: It always is on Mondays. Is that your dog barking in the background earlier on the call?

speaker: Ravi
text: Ha, yes, that's Biscuit, sorry about that.

speaker: Dana
text: No problem. Let's get started. First question: how would you design a rate limiter for a public API?

speaker: Ravi
text: I'd use a token bucket per API key, stored in Redis, so every instance of the service shares the same counters.

speaker: Ravi
text: Each request takes a token, tokens refill at a fixed rate, and when the bucket is empty we return a 429 with a Retry-After header.

speaker: Dana
text: Good. What happens if Redis goes down?

speaker: Ravi
text: I'd fail open with a local in-memory limit as a fallback, so an outage of the limiter doesn't take the whole API down.

speaker: Dana
text: Okay. Second question: a query on the orders table got slow as the table grew. How would you speed it up?

speaker: Ravi
text: Hmm, I'm honestly not sure. Maybe add more memory to the database server? I haven't worked much with database indexes.

speaker: Dana
text: Would an index on the customer id column help here, do you think?

speaker: Ravi
text: I think so, but I couldn't really explain how an index changes the query plan.

speaker: Dana
text: That's fine. Last one: tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.

speaker: Ravi
text: On my last team we disagreed about rewriting a service. I wrote a one-page comparison of both options and we agreed to refactor instead of rewriting.

speaker: Dana
text: Nice, that's a clear example of resolving conflict with data.

speaker: Ravi
text: Thanks. Can I ask when I'll hear back?

speaker: Dana
text: I'll send my feedback to the hiring committee by Thursday, and the recruiter will contact you after that.

speaker: Ravi
text: Great, thank you for your time.

speaker: Dana
text: Thanks Ravi, enjoy the rest of your day.
